text: public GHO directory contains many indicators, single indicator may cover countries years need. issuing full download gho_data(), three lightweight helpers let ask server available without transferring observations. gho_has_data() quick yes / given indicator filter — useful screening list candidate indicators. returns TRUE, FALSE, NA (request failures, including code absent current public directory). gho_count() returns number rows filter produce, useful sizing download. gho_coverage() summarises year coverage observation counts per country. payload small SpatialDim TimeDim requested server.

title: DSIR
text: DSIR provides two paired ggplot2 themes tuned -style charts — clean panels, modest grids, consistent accent colour. Use drop-replacements theme_minimal() theme_bw() respectively whenever chart heading deliverable. rule thumb simple: single-panel plots use theme_dsi(), faceted plots use theme_dsi_facet(). two share typography, title treatment, legend handling, differ frame data — facet variant adds panel borders, light strip backgrounds, breathing room panels, look heavy single-panel chart.

title: DSIR
text: theme_dsi() keeps chart chrome minimal — half-frame axis, light grid lines, -blue accent axis line. default grid runs directions; pass grid = "y" minimalist horizontal-look. bar charts, pair theme_dsi() scale_y_dsi_col() (scale_x_dsi_col() value mapped x) — thin wrappers around scale_*_continuous() remove lower axis expansion, columns sit flush axis instead floating .
code: uhc_clean |>   filter(iso3 %in% c("AUS", "CHN", "PHL", "FJI")) |>   left_join(who_countries, by = "iso3") |>   ggplot(aes(x = year, y = value_num, group = iso3, color = name_short)) +   geom_line(linewidth = .8) +   geom_point(size = 1.8) +   theme_dsi() +   labs(     title    = "UHC Service Coverage Index, selected WPR Member States",     subtitle = "2015 onwards",     x = NULL, y = "SCI", color = NULL   ) uhc_clean |>   filter(year == max(year)) |>   left_join(who_countries, by = "iso3") |>   arrange(desc(value_num)) |>   head(10) |>   ggplot(aes(reorder(name_short, value_num), value_num)) +   geom_col(fill = "#0093D5") +   coord_flip() +   scale_y_dsi_col() +   theme_dsi(grid = "x") +   labs(     title    = "UHC Service Coverage Index, top 10 WPR Member States",     subtitle = "Latest available year",     x = NULL, y = "SCI"   )

title: DSIR
text: chart split across many small panels, half-frame look becomes visually noisy — accent-blue axis line repeats across every facet. theme_dsi_facet() switches full panel border, adds light grey strip background clearly mark facet’s label, introduces panel spacing adjacent panels don’t run together. strip_fill argument lets change strip background colour emphasis — example, light-blue tone derived accent deliverable strips carry meaning:

text: sdg_data() sdg_clean() follow fetch--tidy pattern GHO counterparts. main differences indicator codes use dotted SDG format (e.g. "3.4.1") raw value kept character — SDG API returns non-numeric entries ("<0.1", aggregate notes) rows. cleaned value_num, low, high columns numeric, NA conversion possible. sdg_indicators() accepts optional search argument behaviour gho_indicators() — multiple keywords -ed together matched case-insensitively indicator description. filter runs client-side UN SDG indicator list short (~250 rows) endpoint OData. area argument sdg_data() sdg_coverage() accepts either ISO3 codes (converted internally via iso3_to_m49()) UN M49 numeric codes — DSIR’s regional vectors (wpro_cty, afro_cty, etc.) work directly, way GHO client. mix two formats single call. default, sdg_clean() produces 15-column schema gho_clean(), two outputs can combined directly bind_indicators(). what: Combining GHO and SDG with bind_indicators()
title: DSIR
text: analysis pulls indicators sources, bind_indicators() stacks number cleaned tibbles one. source column ("gho" / "sdg") lets filter facet origin without remembering frame came API. Additional columns, including named SDG dimensions, retained; inputs without columns receive typed missing values. Binding rows harmonise codes definitions across sources.
code: # Two indicators on the same topic from different APIs: #   GHO NCDMORT3070 (probability of premature NCD mortality) #   SDG 3.4.1       (mortality rate from NCDs) gho_ncd <- gho_data("NCDMORT3070", area = wpro_cty) |> gho_clean() sdg_ncd <- sdg_data("3.4.1",        area = wpro_cty) |> sdg_clean() bind_indicators(gho_ncd, sdg_ncd) |> glimpse()

title: DSIR
text: single SDG indicator often contains several series — example different vaccines, sex strata, causes death — country year coverage. Indicator "3.b.1" (vaccine coverage) clear case: published four separate series (DTP3, MCV2, PCV3, HPV), year coverage newer vaccines much shorter DTP3. sdg_coverage() summarises year range observation count per (location, series), can inspect series exist covered deciding one analyse. Note DSIR intentionally provide SDG analogues gho_has_data() gho_count(). SDG data generally complete enough screening helpers add little value — useful pre-analysis question SDG “series available?”, sdg_coverage() answers.

title: Average Annual Rate of Reduction (AARR) — aarr
text: year Numeric vector years. value Numeric vector indicator values, length year. Values must positive (computation log scale); zero negative value yields NA_real_ warning. method Character. "regression" (default) "endpoint". See Details. na.rm Logical. pairs missing year value removed computation? Default TRUE. FALSE, missing element makes result NA_real_.

title: Average Annual Rate of Reduction (AARR) — aarr
text: numeric scalar: average annual rate reduction fraction (0.024 = 2.4% per year). Multiply 100 compare published / UNICEF tables, print percentages. Returns NA_real_ (warning) fewer two distinct years remain NA handling, value zero negative, year value contains non-finite values.

title: Average Annual Rate of Reduction (AARR) — aarr
text: Two estimation methods offered: "regression" (default; UNICEF-recommended approach): ordinary least-squares line fitted log(value) year, AARR 1 - exp(b), b fitted slope. observations contribute, estimate robust noise individual years. "endpoint": earliest latest years used: 1 - (v1 / v0) ^ (1 / (y1 - y0)), v0 v1 values earliest year y0 latest year y1. Intermediate observations ignored. several observations share earliest latest year, mean used (see note duplicated years ). Sign convention. positive AARR means indicator declining (progress, mortality-type indicator): 0.024 means average decline 2.4% per year. negative AARR means indicator increasing. Note reverse growth rate. Duplicated years usually mean data still mix several strata — example sexes plus male / female dim1, several series codes data cleaned gho_clean() / sdg_clean(). aarr() warns proceeds (regression pools strata), almost always want filter single stratum first. Relation published figures. Published / UNICEF tables print AARR percentage (4.4 meaning 4.4% per year); multiply value returned function 100 compare. Note also Trends Maternal Mortality reports print continuous-time rate, -log(v1 / v0) / (y1 - y0) (called ARR), agrees closely exactly discrete AARR computed — small differences tables expected.

title: Average Annual Rate of Reduction (AARR) — aarr
code: # A perfectly exponential 2.4%/yr decline recovers exactly 0.024 years  <- 2000:2015 values <- 100 * (1 - 0.024) ^ (years - 2000) aarr(years, values)                       # 0.024 #> [1] 0.024 100 * aarr(years, values)                 # 2.4 — as printed in reports #> [1] 2.4  # Endpoint method uses only the earliest and latest years aarr(years, values, method = "endpoint")  # also 0.024 here #> [1] 0.024  # An increasing indicator gives a negative AARR aarr(2010:2020, 50 * 1.01 ^ (0:10))       # about -0.01 #> [1] -0.01  # Back-of-envelope projection to 2030 at the observed AARR r <- aarr(years, values) values[length(values)] * (1 - r) ^ (2030 - 2015) #> [1] 48.24969

title: Directly Age-Standardized Rate — age_standardize
text: age-specific rate group \(\) \(r_i = d_i / n_i\) (count / pop). standard weights \(w_i\) (stdpop, normalized sum 1), standardized rate $$R = \left(\sum_i w_i r_i\right) \times \mathrm{per}.$$ three vectors count, pop, stdpop must aligned: element \(\) refers age group, order. stdpop may supplied counts, standard million, percentages — relative values matter, normalized internally. built-who_std_pop dataset supplies 2026 Standard. Confidence interval. ci = TRUE, confidence interval returned using gamma-distribution method Fay Feuer (1997), good coverage even rates based small numbers events. method used , example, epitools. interval requires age-specific event counts, available count pop supplied (pre-computed rate).

title: Directly Age-Standardized Rate — age_standardize
text: World Health Organization (2026). Revised standard population calculating age-standardized rates. /HSA/DDA/GHE/2026.4. Fay MP, Feuer EJ (1997). Confidence intervals directly standardized rates: method based gamma distribution. Statistics Medicine 16(7):791-801.

text: Builds standard period life table age-specific mortality rates (nMx). Works abridged tables (age groups 0, 1, 5, 10, ..., 85+) complete single-year tables (0, 1, 2, ..., 100+); last age group always treated open-ended.

title: Period Life Table from Age-Specific Mortality Rates — life_table
code: life_table(   age,   mx,   sex = c("total", "male", "female"),   ax = NULL,   radix = 1e+05 )

title: Period Life Table from Age-Specific Mortality Rates — life_table
text: age Numeric vector age-group lower bounds, strictly increasing, e.g. c(0, 1, seq(5, 85, = 5)) standard abridged table. last group open-ended. mx Numeric vector age-specific mortality rates (deaths per person-year), length age. Must non-negative, missing values. sex Character. "total" (default), "male", "female". used default infant child ax (see Details). ax Optional numeric vector overriding default person-years assumptions, length age. NA elements fall back defaults. radix Numeric. starting cohort size l0. Default 100000; use 1 survivorship proportions.

title: Period Life Table from Age-Specific Mortality Rates — life_table
text: tibble one row per age group columns: age Age-group lower bound (supplied). n Width age interval; Inf open interval. mx Age-specific mortality rate (supplied). ax Average person-years lived interval dying . qx Probability dying interval; 1 open interval. lx Survivors exact age x radix. dx Deaths interval. Lx Person-years lived interval. Tx Person-years lived exact age x. ex Remaining life expectancy exact age x. NA lx reached 0.

title: Period Life Table from Age-Specific Mortality Rates — life_table
text: conversion mortality rate mx probability dying qx uses standard relation $${}_nq_x = \frac{n \, {}_nm_x}{1 + (n - {}_na_x) \, {}_nm_x},$$ \({}_na_x\) average number person-years lived interval dying . Values qx capped 1 (warning, since capping signals implausibly high rates). open interval, qx = 1 Lx = lx / mx. ax assumption. default: age 0 (first group age 0 width 1): Coale-Demeny West formulas keyed m0 (Preston, Heuveline Guillot 2001, Table 3.3), sex. sex = "total", male female values averaged. ages 1-4 (second group ages 1-4): corresponding Coale-Demeny West formula. closed intervals: n / 2 (midpoint assumption). open interval: 1 / mx (life expectancy implied constant rate). Pass ax vector override , e.g. match published table exactly. Life expectancy tabulated age read ex column: ex[1] life expectancy birth table starts age 0. table may also start age 0 (e.g. age = c(60, 65, ..., 85)) compute remaining life expectancy conditional survival first age.

title: Tidy an SDG Data Frame — sdg_clean
text: df data frame returned sdg_data(). keep_dimensions Logical. Append named SDG dimensions character columns? Default FALSE preserves 15-column format. TRUE, names converted snake_case prefixed dim_, e.g. Age becomes dim_age, Reporting Type becomes dim_reporting_type, Type_of_household becomes dim_type_of_household. Codes kept unchanged; absent values remain NA. Conflicting names conversion cause error. dimensions, total-population codes, GHO component codes inferred. Use sdg_dimensions() look official codes labels. keep_metadata Logical. Retain observation attributes source context? Default FALSE. TRUE, returned attributes become character columns prefixed attr_ (e.g. attr_units, attr_nature). Also appends data_source, time_detail, time_coverage, base_period, value_type, geo_info_url character columns. footnotes, indicator_codes, goal_codes, target_codes list-columns character vectors, preserving entries rather just first. Missing scalar fields NA; missing list fields empty character vectors. option independent keep_dimensions makes extra network requests.
